title: Pawn structure
line: Pawns in groups, called islands. The fewer islands, the fewer weak pawns.

steps.text: Pawns side by side form an island. White has two islands. Black has three, and two of its pawns stand alone.
A pawn with no pawn of its own color on a file next to it can be guarded only by pieces. Tap each Black pawn like that.

wrong.f7: A black pawn stands on the next file.
wrong.g7: Black pawns stand on both sides of it.
wrong.h7: A black pawn stands on the next file.

steps.hint: Look on the side of the board where Black has only two pawns.
steps.after: Both stand alone. No black pawn can guard them now.

steps.text: In an ending the king is a fighter. Walk it toward the lone pawns.

also.c4b4: That heads there too. This lesson goes on with the king next to the pawn on c6.

steps.hint: The king steps up the board, next to one of them.
steps.after: Black's king comes back to guard the pawn on c6.

steps.text: Step in between the two lone pawns. Your king attacks both, and Black's king can guard only one.
steps.hint: The square between them is in front of your king, to the left.
steps.after: Black pushes one pawn away, but it is still alone.
A pawn up. Black's other lone pawn is still a target.

summary: Every pawn island is one more group to guard. A lone pawn can be guarded only by pieces.
